proposed_relationship: Combining mechanical cleavage of layered materials with the knowledge of graphite's structure could lead to the creation of thin, two-dimensional carbon sheets.
mechanism: The mechanical cleavage technique can be applied to graphite, which is composed of stacked two-dimensional layers, to separate these layers into individual or few-layer sheets. This process exploits the weak van der Waals forces holding the layers together in graphite, potentially allowing for the isolation of single or few-layer carbon sheets. These sheets, being strictly two-dimensional, would have unique properties compared to their bulk counterparts, including potentially useful electronic properties similar to those of carbon nanotubes.
constraint_released: The limitation imposed by the thermodynamic instability of strictly two-dimensional crystals at finite temperatures could be mitigated by stabilizing these sheets through interaction with a substrate or by functionalization.
